faults.finding: 'coming back to 0 only for the right currents' is false for one loop: a whole line of pairs brings loop 1 back to 0 (4 A and 0 A does).
faults.fix: Say both loops read 0 only at the pair where their two lines cross.

faults.finding: Names only the total reaching 0, not that it takes both loops together, which is the cause of needing two equations.
faults.fix: Name both loops and the crossing; the action is setting the dials and walking each loop.

faults.finding: 'Battery 1 always gives more current because it is the better battery' gives no mechanism and is a false absolute (a lower-voltage battery 1 could give less).
faults.fix: Both batteries hold the load at 9 V, so each loses 3 V inside: 3 A through 1 Ω, 1.5 A through 2 Ω.

faults.finding: The recommended shape wants the common misconception shown failing; using one loop alone is never shown to fail.
faults.fix: Show 4 A and 0 A bringing loop 1 to 0 while leaving loop 2 at 4 V.

faults.finding: confidence is simplified but the explanation never names the fixed-voltage, fixed-resistance battery as a teaching model.
faults.fix: One closing sentence naming the model.

faults.finding: The brief lists writing the outside loop as a third equation as a slip to check; draft 1 leaves it out.
faults.fix: Add it, with the reason (it is loop 1 take away loop 2).
